Primech Vision coordinates facility workers and multiple robot types

A Singapore headquarters pilot brings delivery, reception and cleaning robots together with HYTRON.

Primech / GlobeNewswire ↗1 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Beyond a single-purpose robot

Primech Holdings introduced Primech Vision on October 1, 2026 to coordinate facility personnel and multiple robot types. A pilot at its Singapore headquarters expands the company’s approach beyond HYTRON, its restroom-cleaning robot, to include delivery, reception and other cleaning robots.

From an issue to a tracked task

Robots, cameras or staff can identify facility issues. The platform converts these into tasks, assigns them to people or robotic systems, and follows execution and completion through a central interface. The aim is to give managers a site-wide view of work rather than separate status displays for individual machines.

Internal testing before broader rollout

Primech plans live demonstrations for visiting customers from Asia, Europe and the United States starting in October. Its internal pilot evaluates workflow integration and human-robot collaboration. The announcement supplies no measured savings or broad deployment results. Exception handling and handoffs to people remain practical points to assess.
